**r01** — Premise is wrong: there is no Redis anywhere in the repo (no Redis client in `go.mod`, no config). Actual mechanism: a process-local in-memory cache, `store/cache/cache.go` (`Cache` struct `:65`, `New` `:75`, backed by `sync.Map` with a background `cleanupLoop`). Three instances are created in `store.New` — `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` — `store/store.go:47-58`, with config `DefaultTTL: 10 * time.Minute`, `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute`, `MaxItems: 1000` (`store/store.go:40-45`). User entries therefore expire after **10 minutes** (they are written via `Set`, i.e. the default TTL — `store/user.go:143,167`), and are also invalidated explicitly on update/delete (`store/user.go:171-181`). Caches are shut down in `Store.Close` (`store/store.go:72-77`).

**r02** — Premise is wrong: there is no per-user (or any) API rate-limiting middleware in this codebase — no limiter dependency in `go.mod` and no registration anywhere. The only Echo middleware registered is `middleware.Recover()` and the CORS middleware (`server/server.go:51-52`); the Connect/gRPC interceptor chain is metadata, logging, recovery, and auth only (`server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go:22,98,165`; authorizer at `server/router/api/v1/v1.go:67`). The nearest throttling constructs are concurrency semaphores for thumbnail/image work (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:59-60`, `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:117`), a 256 MiB request-size cap (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:20`), and the 128-slot bounded webhook queue (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:39`). The only mention of rate limiting is an aspirational comment in `internal/email/doc.go:86`.

**r03** — Premise is wrong: there is no nightly database-cleanup job and no cron scheduler running in production. `internal/scheduler` exists as a self-contained cron package (`internal/scheduler/scheduler.go:54`, `internal/scheduler/parser.go:30`) but it is never instantiated outside its own tests/examples (`grep -rn "scheduler\." --include=*.go` outside `internal/scheduler` returns nothing). The only background work started at startup is the S3 presign runner on a 12-hour ticker (`server/server.go:153-172`, `server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27`). Cleanup of user-owned rows happens transactionally at delete time instead (`store/db/*/user_delete.go`).

**r04** — Premise is wrong: there is no message broker at all — neither NATS nor RabbitMQ (nor Kafka/AMQP) appears in `go.mod` or any source file, and no queue is declared. Actual mechanism: an in-process buffered Go channel, `asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` — `internal/webhook/webhook.go:39` — drained by 4 goroutines started in `init()` (`internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55`); producers call `webhook.PostAsync` (`:184`), which drops the payload with a warning when the buffer is full. Delivery is `webhook.Post` (`:120`). The queue is not persistent — pending deliveries are lost on restart.

**r05** — Premise is wrong: there is no GraphQL schema or GraphQL server in this repo (no `graphql` reference in any Go/TS file or dependency). Actual public API surface: Protobuf-defined gRPC services in `proto/api/v1/*.proto` (generated into `proto/gen/api/v1/`), exposed over HTTP two ways — Connect RPC handlers and a gRPC-Gateway REST/JSON mapping — both registered in `(*APIV1Service).RegisterGateway` (`server/router/api/v1/v1.go:65`) and mounted in `server/server.go:88`. Additional non-gRPC surfaces: SSE (`server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go`), the HTTP file server at `/file/...` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:122-125`), RSS feeds (`server/router/rss/rss.go`), MCP (`server/router/mcp`, `server/server.go:91`), and `/healthz` (`server/server.go:65`).
